title: Scalable Learning of Non-Decomposable Objectives
authors: Elad Eban, Mariano Schain, Alan Mackey, Ariel Gordon, Ryan Rifkin, Gal Elidan
venue: Proceedings of the 20th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS), PMLR vol. 54
conclusions: Introduces simple 'building block' bounds on per-example true-positive/false-positive indicator quantities (via hinge-loss upper/lower bounds) that let a wide range of non-decomposable, rank-based objectives be optimized with standard stochastic gradient descent.

Casts constrained objectives such as maximum recall at fixed precision (R@P) and maximum precision at fixed recall (P@R) as a Lagrangian saddle-point problem over dataset-level tp/fp aggregate counts, solved by primal-dual SGD.
Extends the same bounds to approximate AUCPR (via a discretized R@P integral over precision anchor points) and to the F_beta score.

All objectives are dataset/mini-batch aggregate rate quantities computed over a training distribution and optimized inductively (to generalize to new data), not verified against a fixed, already-realized test set.

Empirically validated at scale (CIFAR-10, ImageNet, and Google's internal JFT with 300M+ images), showing consistent AUCPR/P@R/R@P gains over accuracy-trained (softmax) and AUCROC-surrogate baselines with no meaningful loss of scalability.
our_use: main.tex:181-182, in the 'Rate-constrained learning' related-work paragraph: '...non-decomposable rate objectives through surrogate bounds \citep{eban2017scalable}...These bound expected rates over a distribution, inductively. Our requirement is a hard count on one specific test set: transductive, verified on the argmax predictions themselves, and paired with per-group local caps.' The paper is cited as the representative example of optimizing non-decomposable rate objectives via convex surrogate bounds, contrasted with our transductive, single-test-set hard count constraint.
